items.name: 15x Critical kush grow
items.grow_notes:
Hello guys!

This is my 3rd grow, and this time I'm going to record it all on here. My first grow was 3x OG kush and 3x barneys blue cheese - in coco and under 600w hps, yield was 12oz dry.

2nd grow was 4 blue cheese clones (15l pots, coco, 600 hps) yield was 18oz dry.

Now I've just cracked 15 Critical kush seeds, and I've bought a lovely new T5 4ft 8tube for seedlings. I will use metal halide thru vegging and then hps for bloom. I'm using coco/perlite mix at 70/30. Tent size is 1.5m x 3.0m x 2.0m.

I'm wondering how much light I will need through vegging and bloom. I'm thinking maybe 1500-2000w?? The strain info says 750g per m2, which would be over 1500g. But then on my last grow I achieved 0.75g per watt. How much light will I need to maximise yield? Any questions, input or advice would be most appreciated :-) 

Photos of last projects as well as pics of this current one will be uploaded soon.........

items.name_norm: 3 finger leaves and claw stunted flowering might be half auto or hermie father
items.thread_title: 3 finger leaves and claw, stunted flowering. Might be half auto or hermie father
items.grow_notes:
Upper leaves of 2 of my plants are growing 3 finger leaves with claws and they look very unhealthy. These 2 plants are the tallest ones, during flowering stretch their upper leaves grew taller than the hood, so they couldn't get light. Supercrop didn't stop them, they got 6.6 feet so I go vertical and bend and tied them.

After asking google, I learned that re-vegging and heat stress is the most common reason of 3 finger leaves and unfortunately both these two reasons might happen to me. These are supposed to be autoflowers and I always go with 16+8 light schedule. 3 weeks ago they get started to flower under 16+8 but a week later flowering seems stopped. Can autoflowers re-veg by the way?

After switching vertical, the upper part of grow room got hotter because flooded tube pulls air from down and upper parts mostly stays hot. But still the only thing these affected leaves have in common is that they were taller than the hood and didn't get much light.

items.name: 8" deep X 6" diam. pots with 17 day old seedlings/probable over watering 1X
items.name_norm: 8 deep x 6 diam pots with 17 day old seedlings probable over watering 1x
items.thread_title: 8" deep X 6" diam. pots with 17 day old seedlings/probable over watering 1X
items.grow_notes:
Ok , normally I would let seedlings grow in plastic cups until they were well filled with roots then transplant. But I have them now 17 days old in larger pots, 8 X 6 diamter. Slightly curled or bent downward nothing crazy. Light seems good no burn, 75F at canopy top. WEll drained soil. Question, they did seem to pop back up and look better after 4 days of no water. Top 4 inches I let dry out, so half the pot. NOt sure how much I should even rely on soil moisture tester probe. SO from 5" down to 8" bottom the tester read "wet" fairly dry down to 4" Question is I think the 4 days was a bit too long to wait, should I let them bottom 3/4 of soild dry out almost completely? I tend to think NOT, or use my tester and go 3 days and it should be roughly 3" of dry soil on top. I did put more water around the seedlings and near base than normal. Should I let it dry out for over a weeek? as long as they look ok? Soil is not WET by any means its damp to my fingers touching, its the tester that says "wet" 

I feel like I'll just wait til top 3-4" are DRY to touch and tester, then use my old pill container to water just near base a couple times and done. I feel it will penetrate maybe 3-4" max.

items.excerpt:
ABF Genetics – Official Rollitup Seedbank Thread​ What's up everyone,

I'm Ghost , founder of ABF Genetics , established in Oakland, California in 2010 .

Like many of you, I came up through the forums, hunting through seed packs, preserving elite cuts, and making selections that I thought deserved to stick around.

Over the years, I've been fortunate enough to play a role in preserving and distributing several cultivars that later became highly influential.

Among them was helping source and spread what eventually became known as the Forum Cut Girl Scout Cookies , as well as distributing the original Do-Si-Dos keeper phenotype that later became widely known as the NorCal Do-Si-Dos cut after NorCal from ICMag.

ABF Genetics focuses on preservation work, clone-only reversals, and making hybrids from selections that have a story behind them.

Some projects people may recognize include Azazel , which was discussed on The Pot Cast Podcast , and our Atomic Tangerine from the Runtz reversal project , which was later utilized by CV 420 and Black Tuna Seeds in the creation of Toronjaz .

More recently, much of our attention has shifted toward Hawaiian Sherb Cake , a project built around a personally selected Federation Hawaiian F2 #15 paired with a reversed (Wedding Cake × Sunset Sherbert) . It has become one of our favorite lines to work with thanks to its tropical floral profile, creamy undertones, and uplifting, non-anxious effect that many have described as feeling like a spa day in flower form .

Current work also includes projects involving Orange Zkittlez , Z Cube , and a selected Zkittlez × Sour Dubb reversal from original Melting Pot Farm stock.

We'll also be exhibiting at Expo Cannabis Argentina (October 2026) and in Expo Cannabis Brasil (November 2026) .

This thread will be used to share:

• Upcoming releases

• Flower and hash photos

• Grow reports

• Event announcements

• Promotions and giveaways

Questions, grow reports, smoke reports, and constructive criticism are always welcome.

Thanks for stopping by and supporting preservation breeding.

For more information check out Always Be Flowering 

— Ghost 

 ABF Genetics​ Established 2010 • Oakland, California 

 Preserving Yesterday. Breeding Tomorrow.

items.name: Acid snow “speed run seeds”
items.grow_notes:
Just chopped my acid snow at day 75 . I stunted these autos somewhere along the line with the “new to me “ canna coco nutes , and autopot system .

This one checks all the boxes so far ! Amazing terps , very dense , easy to trim , and huge buds on a tiny 30” plant . In quality hands , this plant would grow some amazing flower with some crazy high yields for sure . 

If you’re on the fence about trying some speedrun gear , I suggest pulling the trigger . 

I’ll check back with a smoke report in a week or two . I usually pull a tester when dry , then cure for 3-5 weeks in mason jars

items.thread_title: Any tips on not being a seed whore??
items.grow_notes:
There's still a few 4/20 sales going on, and it's so very tempting to fill up the shopping carts. 

It's all I can do to keep myself under control

I have enough genetics to keep me busy for probably years, since I do moms and clones. I don't grow packs but one or two of a strain at a time and if I find a keeper I run it till something better shows up. As you can imagine, this doesn't leave alot of room for new genetics to pop in. Limited room, limited power, limited time. I also wanna do some of my own crosses. 

So how do you maintain sanity when there's just SOOOOO much out there?

items.name: Anybody using a trolmaster aqua-x PLUS - nfs3?
items.name_norm: anybody using a trolmaster aqua x plus nfs3
items.thread_title: Anybody using a trolmaster aqua-x PLUS - nfs3?
items.grow_notes: Title says it, wondering if there are any TM users out there that can tell me something good about the aqua-x, particularly the nfs3 ie PLUS version. is it less finicky than the nfs1s. Do the wcs sensors stay calibrated, and which is more accurate, the wcs1 or wcs2? I have an NFS 1 and it was a lil buggy at first, big learning curve, not a user friendly plug n play unit in the calibration dept. At least not in unislabs. But after a while it's proven usefull. I just need more sensors and am thinking the wcs1's cuz they're cheap enough on the bay and an NFS3 cuz I really only want to read 6 wcs sensors individually. I know, I know, pulse, growlink etc but at 400$ a sensor that's $2400 just in sensors. At $130/ea the wcs1's would be under 700 cuz i only need 5 more and the controller is about $11-$1200. TM stuff is much cheaper to expand..& MUCH MUCH MUCH easier to get. Local shop even has some TM stuff. Sensors all over ebay, I'm fully aware there may be a good reason for that. So who's got an Aqua-x PLUS and would they buy it again? Thanks!

items.name: Auto, or is it?
items.grow_notes:
I only grow indoors. I prefer the controlled environment. Every summer I try one outdoors among my tomatoes. Usually ends up a flop for a variety of reasons. Short NE growing season, too much rain, wind.

Here's one of my fav strains. Wedding Cheesecake by 420 Fastbuds. But is it? Could it be a photo in disguise?

Notice the timeline on the photos. No explosive growth like you often see in autos. Plant was started indoors. 600w MH. Soil was a 50/50 mix of FFOF and coco. Placed outdoors on 6/14.

Since I placed it outdoors all it's done is stretch. If you look closely it just went into flower. I still have 2.5 months left in my growing season so we'll see.

First photo is 6/14, second is 6/20, third is today ( my birthday) 7/10.

items.name: Auto (Quick One) looks like it’s revegging? Planted October 2025
items.name_norm: auto quick one looks like it s revegging planted october 2025
items.thread_title: Auto (Quick One) looks like it’s revegging? Planted October 2025
items.grow_notes:
Hey everyone,

I’m a bit confused about what’s going on with one of my plants and wanted some experienced opinions.

This was sold as an autoflower — Quick One from Royal Queen Seeds. I planted it back in October 2025, so it’s been alive way longer than a normal auto cycle.

It’s growing indoors on my varanda (balcony), but I’m not using any artificial light — just natural sunlight it gets during the day.

I also planted it pretty casually, with the mindset that if it grows it grows, and if it doesn’t that’s fine.

It started flowering and has buds with white pistils, but at the same time I’m getting really weird new growth:

Thin / twisted leaves

Some single-blade or irregular leaves

Bright green shoots coming out of bud sites

To me it actually looks like a reveg, but I thought autos don’t reveg.

So now I’m not sure what I’m dealing with:

Is this actually revegging somehow?

Or just a stressed autoflower doing something weird (foxtailing, etc)?

Also unsure what to do next:

Should I prune the buds and try to push veg?

Or just leave it and let it finish as-is?

I can post more pics if needed, but I’ve attached a few showing the structure and new growth.

Any help appreciated

items.name: Barney's farm Scam Seeds
items.grow_notes:
I bought 10 Gorilla Z seeds directly from Barney’s Farm, and 4 of them turned out completely defective due to clear genetic problems. One sprouted without cotyledons, another had only one and stayed weak, and two died under the soil because of overly thick shells. 

I contacted the company several times, asking politely for a fair solution and even offered to return the unused seeds. They refused to take responsibility and only sent me a 30% discount code for my next order which is meaningless since I will never order again. 

After that, they stopped replying completely. I gave them two chances to fix this and warned them I would file an official complaint. They ignored everything. 

I have now officially reported the case to the **European Consumer Centre (EVZ Germany / ECC-Net)** and provided photos, invoices, and all emails as evidence. 

Extremely poor customer service and very disappointing genetic quality. Definitely not recommended.

items.name_norm: best temperature and humidity from seed to smoke
items.thread_title: Best Temperature and Humidity from seed to Smoke.
items.grow_notes:
Hey Y'all 

It's been a minute since I've posted.

Here is what I feel is the best temp and humidity conditions from day One.

Yes, I know about VPD, etc.

Clones- humidity dome @80° and 85% humidity- until roots appear.

Seedling/small plants-,day 1 to 14 

80° and 80% humidity.

Remainder of growth- 80° and 60% humidity.

Flower- weeks 1-2

80° and 55% humidity.

Weeks 3-4

75° and 50% humidity 

Weeks 5-6

70° and 45% humidity 

Weeks 7+

65° and 40% humidity 

Drying- 14 days at 60° and 60% humidity 

Curing- Terp bags 

Or Jars with 62% humidity packs, burped 5 minutes for 7 days, 1 minute for 14 days. 

Anyone else use similar techniques with great results?

BLUE DREAM Humboldt Seed Organization 

Blueberry x haze

Flower in 9 weeks

HOLY GRAIL KUSH DNA Genetics 

kosher x OG #18

Flower in 9 weeks

OK, so this was my first time growing out blue dream and my second run at holy grail kush. I started the BD from seed and the HGK is a clone from my last grow which was some pretty good bud that reeked of some funky (good funky) OG! Now each of these were vegged for a bit over 2 months. I grew them in a 2'×3'×5' grow tent under a 400w MH. I'm using Moonshine Man Mix organic soil to grow these in. Go organics! When they each had about 5 fan leaves I topped them once. Then LST'D, super cropped, and did some more topping to even out and open up their canopy. And finally I transplanted the HGK into a 7 gal pot and the BD into a 10 gal pot, let there roots stretch for another week and moved them to the flowering room. My flower closet is 3'x4'x8' and lined with panda film and hung over my plants is a wing hooded bare bulb 600w HPS on 12/12. Currently the HGK is at day 29 in flower. BD is at day 21 where I have today done a little bit of a lollipop on her to fatten up the buds and get rid of the small popcorn nugs. Fairly new to lollipoppin so hopefully I did OK and she grows without a stunt! Temps usually stay around 75°F with lights on and drop about 10°F when lights are off. RH staying around 30% during flower. And that's about all now for now. Will post pictures tomorrow! Thanks for looking. Peace.

items.name: ChemDawg, OG Kush, Triangle Kush, Kush Mints
items.name_norm: chemdawg og kush triangle kush kush mints
items.thread_title: ChemDawg, OG Kush, Triangle Kush, Kush Mints
items.grow_notes:
After growing 40+ strains from multiple breeders over the past 4 to 5 years, I've only really enjoyed strains with genetics that include some combo of ChemDawg, OG Kush, (which includes ChemDawg), Kush Mints, and/or Triangle Kush in hybrids that don't include so many other strains that they drown out the influence of these four.

If I'm wrong, what am I missing?

If you line up all 40+ strains, some deliver effects that I can only describe as a "flat" high, others are "noisy," or, worse, effects that make me ask "where are my keys"? If, for example, the high is flat, more or less THC isn't going to change that -- more THC would amp it up but, overall, the effects are flat.

I enjoy and continue to search for strains that deliver a clear up or down high (maybe even spaced out if indica-dominant, but not couch-lock).

And I realize 40+ strains is still a relatively small sample, but I'm not throwing away as much money on seeds of strains that don't deliver.

items.grow_notes:
I have a cross Idea I would love to see someone with the knowledge and skills run with. Ill give you the break down and you can do with it whatever you wish, all I ask is if any of you do breed it out, send me some seeds lol.

First cross: Green Crack auto x Durban Poison

Second cross : Chocolope x Sour Diesel Auto

Third Cross : White Widow Auto x Jack Herer

Four Cross: Pineapple Express Auto x Purple Thai

Select which ever plant you would want for male and female on these four then take the offspring of cross one and two and cross them and the Off spring of three and 4 and cross them, and then do one final cross with the off spring of those two. Might just be a crazy newbie pipe dream, but I think the final product at the end of the "Breeding bracket" would be an Awesome plant.

I Hope to try this once I get a few years growing under my belt but I am happy to let someone else use the Idea.

items.excerpt:
Hallo everyone,

Hope you’re all having a good season. I’m currently at Day 102 with an auto-run, and I’ve hit a bit of a crossroads. I have two plants that are right at the finish line, but my third an F1 Cosmic Cheddar seems to be on a completely different timeline. I’d love to get some veteran eyes on this to see if I should pivot my strategy.

The Setup:

• Age: Day 102 (Week 15) from sprout.

• Light Cycle: 19/5 (LED).

• Environment: 20.4°C (Min) – 28°C (Max). Rare peaks of 33°C.

• Medium: Soil / Organic Mix.

Full Nutrient Stack:

• Base: Plagron Terra Bloom & Terra Grow.

• Additives: Advanced Nutrients (Overdrive, Big Bud, Bud Candy, Tasty Terpenes).

• Flush/Finish: Flawless Finish (AN) & Green Sensation (Plagron - ready for the Queen).

• Supplements: Canna CalMag (used every watering) + BioBizz CalMag arriving tomorrow.

The "Finished" Pair: Bruce & Cookies

• Status: Peak Maturity. Trichomes are 95% Milky, ~5% Amber. Pistils 80% orange/receded.

• Visuals: Seeing some nice deep Purple/Burgundy hues on the sugar leaves.

• Plan: Final heavy feed (Overdrive/Bud Candy) this Tuesday. Starting Flawless Finish on Saturday using 10°C Ice Water to trigger color/resin, since I can't do a 48h dark period with the other plant still in the tent.

The "Stuck" Queen: F1 Cosmic Cheddar (RQS)

• Status: Late Stretch / Early Bloom.

• The Issue: At Day 102, she’s still stretching with only white pistil "buttons" and no frost yet.

• Symptoms: "Lime green" tops under intensity, but she returns to a healthy dark green when the lights are off. Suspect phototoxicity/light saturation at the ceiling. Currently under soft LST to manage height.

A few questions for the community:

1. F1 Genetics: Has anyone seen a Cosmic Cheddar F1 run this long (100+ days) and still be in early bloom? Is this a "Super-Auto" phenotype or did I potentially get a photoperiod seed in the pack?

2. Light Cycle Flip: Should I stay the course with 19/5, or does she need 12/12 to flip properly despite being an Auto?

3. The "Lime" Color: Given she greens up at night, do you agree it’s just light saturation at the canopy, or does she look like she’s begging for a heavy N/Mg boost at this size?

4. Ice Flush: Without the option for darkness, do you think the 10°C cold-water flush will be enough of a thermal shock to maximize the bag appeal on the Bruce & Cookies?

Thanks in advance for any insights or "sanity checks" you can provide. Much appreciated!

Well, its 2023, and I figured with my next cycle, Ill start a new thread as so much of my grow style is about to change. Probably some of the biggest indoor changes Ive done in a decade. Ive been doing soil...well a long time now. But at my current rental, the workflow with soil isn't working for me. So much mess, and lugging plants and heavy pots around is no longer something I want, as double hernia repair already happened.

So...My next chapter...

I've been gathering parts, but long story short, I will be setting up one of my 5x5 tents with a 4 site RDWC system. I'm going to plumb it myself, but for all intents and purposes, its a current culture setup. I am using their 13 gallon buckets, with a 13 gallon epicenter rez. My current run is still a month out from harvest, so Its still in the plotting and planning phases, but soon enough!

My general plan for this tent will be for pollination projects of my top 4 strains. With less space then I typically have had over the less 15 years to do my typical level of pheno hunting / breeding / crosses etc, Ive decided focus on my absolute best, and let others handle working with cookies and hype.

So, my first run I plan to have the 4 plants as:

Blackberry Moonshine Bx1

Blackberry Moonshine #12

Modified Macberry Moonshine

Haole Moonshine #13 or possibly the chem 91 VA cut or my cherry pie x mac dragon, I haven't 110% decided on that last slot yet.

This first cycle in the current culture will be interest for sure, I plan to do a short veg, and flip, with the tent next to it housing which Blackberry Moonshine bx1 male(s) I select to seed the CC run.

Depending on how things go, I may convert the second tent over to RDWC as well, but will have to see how the maiden run goes.

Nute wize, Im pretty certain Im going to run the Vegaflora nutrient line, as several people Ive been inspired by use it and swear by its ph stability and with their RDWC they all said it takes very little ppms, and they dont get the bio film, algae growth, or any gunk building up in their system.

My paramount concerns with swapping over - I don't want to lug pots and hand water anymore. I want to be able easily keep the room, and tents, and work areas, pristinely clean, and I want to reduce mess and waste.

So anyway - Since no thread is complete with out some photos...

items.name: Elev8 Inc. Review
items.grow_notes: I have not posted here in a long time but my experience with Elev8 Inc. has given no other option but to warn others. I ordered a small order from Elev8 to see if they might be a viable option for diversifying strains to help the Veterans' group I assist. First order arrived within 2 weeks. The problem was it was not what I ordered. After emailing them they responded within a day and told me that they would ship out the correct order as soon as possible. Two weeks later it arrives. The seeds were small and a few were pale. The initial water dunk showed only 40% of them sank within 2 minutes. After germinating them in spite of my skepticism only 75% germinated. I have been sending multiple emails to them and for over 3 weeks have been getting the run-around about Elev8 living up to their guarantee. I am tired of playing this stupid game and will chock this up to a learning experience; I will never use Elev8 again.

However, the plant in question has become lighter and lighter green over the past 2 weeks and has formed brown spots on a few middle-upper canopy leaves and is slowly spreading from the top down to older growth. I have also noticed lower leaf yellowing. She is being kept as follows: Light intensity: 700 PPFD (LEDs), Schedule: 18/6, Temp: 75-80F, RH: 50-60%, Oscillating fan: yes, Soil: FFOF, Nutes: (fox farm trio & cal-mag at half strength every other watering in pH balanced tap water as of 1 week ago). I did a runoff test yesterday using distilled water and the affected plant read 768 ppm @ 6.4 pH. The others that appear much healthier read out at similar values. Is she sick? Is she hungry? Locked out? I’m having a hard time narrowing it down and am looking for some real help. If you need more info or pics please let me know. Thanks for all the input!!

I’ve also got various PH testing kits, and PH adjust.

I have fans inside the tent for air circulation. I have a 4 inch passive air duct. No intake air fan.

items.name: First Grow - White Widow Fem
items.grow_notes:
Hello all,

This is my FIRST grow and first post. Im 3 weeks into flowering (week 9) so I will post the info up to this point.

Started two seeds using “water soak” method and they tailed in about 2 days. Took seedlings to about 6” tall using two dome lamps with 6500k CFL bulbs before I picked the healthier/stronger looking one as I am only in a 3x3 tent. Using a 450w LED and planted in an “Air Pot” using Roots Organic. Topped and trained the plant using the 4-way LST method to get 4x main colas and using a SCROG net. Using forced filtered air in and forced carbon filter out. The seeds I got came with multi phase nutrient bundle so I have just been following that schedule with the addition of CalMag every feeding. I have the pot sitting on a rack so it can drain into a catch pan for easy disposal. Kept temps around 75-80 during “light on” and about 65-70 during “lights out”. Humidity has been kept about 45%-50% the entire time.

Im near the end of week 3 of flowering, total it has been 9 weeks since the sprout was planted. I have roughly 50 bud sites or so and have trimmed the lower hidden bud sites to promote more growth in the exposed ones. Expecting a decent harvest!

items.excerpt:
Decided to start a journal just for the here and now, it'd be nice to have a place to come post pics and stuff again. I did my first journal (in my sig) from february to june/july of this year. Had a great time with it and haven't stopped growing at all, just stopped posting it a lot on rollitup, the in-between time from then to now wasn't all that exciting either, some crappy genetics no doubt. (thanks, th seeds, the third time in person I've seen your genetics put out crap, after sage and kushage) For anybody that followed the first journal though, I did reveg my wonderful starbud from hortilab seeds, which to this day is the best weed I've seen still on the plant in person. 

So onto the real intro-

the setup-

flowering-

5'x5'x7'9" gorilla grow tent

two sun system LEC 315 CMH fixtures 

8 inch phresh hyper fan for exhaust

6 inch vortex s-line fan for intake from outside (only when lights are on)

veg-

4'x4'x7'7" gorilla lite line grow tent

two area 51 RW-75s (white leds switched on only) 

two foot, four bulb t5 ho fixture (soon to be removed)

two area 51 4000k w90s (ordered them a week ago, shouldn't be long now, but not here yet, these will replace the t5)

6 inch vortex s-line fan for exhaust

I started out using this "moonshine mix" from batch 64 as my medium, It seriously is advertised toward pot growers in colorado, and it could be the store I was getting it at, but I got fungus gnats straight out of the bag like every time. I switched to roots organic original blend bought from a different store, and overall it looks and feels like a better soil anyway. also noticeably no bugs. there's still a few gallons of the moonshine mix in my garden, but it's all buried under roots organic since transplanting everything.

I also started out using smart pots, I still like em, but wanted to try with something less... flexible, for lack of a better word. I grabbed some rootmaker pots, which I love so far, but it's really shitty that they don't come in a size larger than about 5 gallons. Because of that, I picked up some 25 liter hercules pots (about 6.6 gallons) which I have a couple of plants in. As I expected though, I'm not a huge fan of the enormous aeration holes. I can see how it depends on the medium, but I don't see it really working out long term for me, I gotta start trying airpots, though they look like a pain in the ass. 

I started out using the bio-canna nutrient line, and adding 4ml of general organics CaMg+ per gallon each feeding, this is what I'm still doing. Thinking about switching to biobizz, or going nuts with it, there's a new nutrient made here in my town called "mammoth p" that I wanna try. They say to use it the full cycle, though more in flower, and that it's pretty much phosphorus and microbes. 

Without further ado, here are some pictures of the here and now-

Starbud, the original plant from my first journal, revegged and flowered. By the way, sometime during the first journal I named this plant, even though I always thought it was really stupid when people would post pictures like "matilda isn't doing so well" or "sarah's getting nice and fat"

but I can't look at this plant and not say the name "Frostithicus"

I still plan on posting in thumpers "Open show and tell" thread, because that's where all the cool outdoor kids hang out.

%100 germination, 20 out of 20.

The first row of five on the left, Lemon Star; Lemon Tree x Sensi Star, AK Bean Brains.

Second row to the left, Candyman Skunk; Candyman Haze x Red Russian Skunk, KOS.

Next row of five, Pine Tar Kush IBL. Got it from AK Bean Brains but I believe it is Tom Hill stock.

Last row, on the right, Boggle Dragon F2; Boggle Gum(BOG) x Blue Dragon, KOS.

She's smelling very strong so far.

items.excerpt:
I've been a lurker for a long time now and figured It might be a good idea to finally start a jounal

Sold some packs the past couple weeks, and thought to myself wow I'm surprised people bought my packs without knowing me or at least following my journal, and I probably would've been a little reluctant to deal with anyone without a journal out of fear of being scammed like I have in the past so here is my journal

I started growing my own veggies when covid hit due to fear of starvation, end of times, apocalypse etc...

What happened was I realized that growing veggies indoors under LEDs was a lot more expensive than just buying them at the farmers market, but from this short lived veggie farming hobby weed growing was born. Was taking bags of trash out to the alley and noticed my neighbors recycling can and a few advanced nutrient bottles sitting on top. Naturally I asked the neighbor about them which he automatically got super defensive and weird about, and he eventually trusted me with his little secret and showed me a few things. Started out like everyone else growing white label garbage, and growing auto flowers and failing until I discovered the instagram bag appeal breeders that sell herm gear. Then eventually met a few older growers on a few forums that turned me onto Bodhi, CSI, Strayfox, High and Lonesome and many others and it opened up a vast world possibilities. Out of the breeders listed Bodhi was the one that I gravitated towards because I had tried the sunshine 4 strain at a dispensary and it quickly became my smoke of choice and I just had to get my hands on seeds to grow it myself. As the years went on I came to learn that the sunshine 4 cut from the dispensary and the one that won the cup is actually Chem 3 x SSDD, but I'm sure I will find something special in these everything I've grown with Chem 4 in it has been fantastic. I belong to a Bodhi preservation group on another forum and most of my grow time is spent trying to preserve packs created by Bodhi seeds

The previous reproductions I've done are Jabba's stash, and Purple Sunshine, and I've done some minor breeding work with a lemon wookie f4 and a 88g13hp male and the f2 seeds are currently being hunted and then I will be working on f3s.

The current seed run right now is Sunshine 4. I was able to obtain a half pack on here a few years ago, and a friend was kind enough to donate his 8 seeds so I had 14 seeds. the reproduction is currently at day 7 after the flip, so I should have a good idea of what ratio I'm gonna get in a few days.

Upcoming seed reproductions after the Sunshine 4 are Skywalker OG x Wookie, Chem 91 x 88g13hp, Topanga pure kush x Wookie, and Pura Vida F3

items.name: Harvest   new caledonia, dinachem x malawi regs sog osmocote positive pressure tent
items.name_norm: harvest new caledonia dinachem x malawi regs sog osmocote positive pressure tent
items.thread_title: Harvest   new caledonia, dinachem x malawi regs sog osmocote positive pressure tent
items.grow_notes:
set up my clone tent 2x2 for this new grow, found some new caledonia seeds at the back of my fridge and i’ve been eyeing that dina malawi cross for a while now so here it goes. 

soaked in paper towels, taproots showing on most (surprising as the new caledonia was preserved very badly so wouldn’t be surprised if none pokes its head). transplanted into about 2lt of garden mix very coco heavy and a lot of aeration. just added 3/4 tsp of osmocote to each pot.

started them under 24hrs on till all above soil, then one week of 18/6 and then 12/12. after sexing them will cull the males maybe gather pollen from the best new caledonia and set up a drip system for the girls. hoping to finish just by watering as osmocote is pretty strong fertilizer and takes a long time to run out. i chose osmocote for this grow bc in these pot sizes its not viable to do organics ime.

also running the tent with positive pressure because it gives me more space for the time being and i recirculate air in the room so 5 carbon filters i have in the same room scrub the air of any smells.

anyway here goes nothing.

items.name: Harvest   The M.M.S. Journal
items.name_norm: harvest the m m s journal
items.grow_notes:
Welcome to the My Memory Sucks journal..

As the title states, the older I get the worse I get at remembering everything throughout my grows. Adding to that I normally take a break from growing during the summer months and it feels like right when I get back into the groove of things it's time to shut everything back down and by the time summer is over I've reverted back to a noob who can't remember what ec, temps etc. was working well.

This year my wife has to go through 2 separate hip replacements so we won't really be doing much this summer. This means I'll finally be running a perpetual grow throughout 2026!

Along with that, I think after all these years I'm finally starting to figure out what setups work best for my spaces.

After 4 years of trying to make leds work, I've come to realize I just can't keep the environment right without majorly supplementing heating in my space since I'm in a basement that stays 68F year round. So I've decided to use a mix of some of the lights I have available.

I have also just recently started using Maxibloom after using various Jacks products over the years along with GH trio and a couple others. I decided just to go with it during flower

After 4 years of trying to make leds work, I've come to realize I just can't keep the environment right without majorly supplementing heating in my space since I'm in a basement that stays 68F year round. So I've decided to use a mix of some of the lights I have available.

I have also just recently started using Maxibloom after using various Jacks products over the years along with GH trio and a couple others. I decided just to go with it during flower since I've never been happy with Jacks in flower, but Im still planing to use my Jacks Tap during veg since Ive always had great results with it.

I've been working the last few weeks to setup one side of the basement for 2 of the 3 tents. I'm pretty happy with how it's come together.

items.excerpt:
Back in mid-March, I inherited some plants in the wake of my friend's breakup. The plants were gnatty, spindly, and stretched as all get-out. I gladly took them in as a quarantine project. I’m a novice gardener, and this is my first cannabis grow.

They were germinated in late-January in 1.75 gal pots in a mixture of Miracle-Gro Seed Starting Potting Mix and something else we can’t remember (in a white bag, peat moss based, maybe EarthGro). Under previous care, they were getting ~1cup of regular tap water once or twice a day in a humid house, sitting six feet beneath a 45w LED. They are believed to be King Louis or Cotton Candy Cane, or KingLouis x CottonCandyCane.

For the first two watering's, I added Miracid 30-10-10 at the full 1.5tbsp/gallon dose because the leaves were yellow and it was what I had. I actually think it did some good. Then I did all this research, got all sorts of supplies, tossed the unsuccessful plants, and babied the survivors. I aimed to build their weak, flimsy stems into strong stalks using an oscillating stand-up fan and a newly purchased 1200w LED light (Exlenvce brand) on an 18/6 schedule. My room was pretty humid at this time, ~60-70% humidity. I had fungus gnat problems for a long time, which I remedied with diatomaceous earth, fans, and yellow sticky cards. The soil was compact with poor drainage. I think I watered every 5-10 days, 1 gallon per pot, using Fox Farm Big Bloom and Grow Big at 25%-50% recommended doses. They grew strong, and I LST’d and supercropped them into an even canopy. It was so rewarding to see them go from pitiful to thriving. Last week’s watering, I used the FF and added 50% recommended dose of Cal-Mag to the water in an effort to remedy what I suspected to be a calcium deficiency.

I transplanted on April 15th. After taking them out, it was apparent that they were moderately root bound in their old plastic pots. There were still some fertilizer balls left from the Miracle-Gro soil. So I tapped off the bottom hunks of soil (maybe 40%) until the lowest two inches of roots were visible, before transplanting into 5 gallon Vivosun fabric pots with a new amended soil:

- 45% Recipe 420 Potting Soil

- 33% Perlite

- 20% Earthworm Castings

- 2% Bone Meal 4-12-0

After transplanting, I gave each plant 4 gallons of plain water at 5.8-6.5pH. I collected some runoff in jars, and then used that to water too. I meant to flush out nutrients. One of them, which received the most runoff of the 4, was drooping today from overwatering. Looking back now, I figure it's better not to re-water with runoff when trying to flush, as it kinda defeats the purpose. Ah well, hindsight is 20/20.

On April 16th, the grow tent came in the mail! I also found a house dehumidifier in my garage -- a god-send. The next day, I switched to a 12/12 light schedule out of fear the plants would outgrow the tent if left in veg for too long. Now the canopy is an even 16 inches, and the plants are straight chilling in their 5x2.5ft Plant House, at a stable 78F and 50% humidity. :D The nighttime temperature I've seen has been 68F, so hopefully I can get the nugs to be a pretty purple.

Today, I have identified signs of fungus gnats and other unknown pest damage. I used the garden hose to spray off whatever I could. Read: https://www.rollitup.org/t/identify-this-bug.1013167/ I have also taken off the plant ties to reduce stress after transplant + shifting to the 12/12 light schedule.

As it stands, I'm not sure how "hot" or nutrient dense my new soil really is, so I plan to play it by ear. I’ll water normally at 6.5pH and I think I won’t add nutrients until I see symptoms of deficiency...

I'm super excited to see how my hard work will turn out! Open to all comments, advice etc!

<3 crittertime

items.name: Inkognyto genetics
items.grow_notes:
Hey. Im a disgruntled buyer. So my story. I got some sensi star f2s from inkognyto via dcseed exchange. I also had my own seeds, some next generation seed co seeds etc. I started all of them the same way i always do. Water for 24 to 36 hours then paper towel in a baggy. All other seeds had germination rates of 90 to 100 percent. Inkognytos 10 pack half failed to germinate, and the other 5 opened but stalled and never grew a tail on the seed, put some in dirt also, none popped up. 

Upon talking to the vendor, they blamed it on my own errors. Been doing this for like 20 years. All other seeds i started same variables etc SPROUTED AND MADE A PLANT. Only their seeds didnt work. All 10. So instead of offering to send me some more seeds, they said it was probably my fault or something. Same variables. Same methods. Only their seeds didnt work. Steer clear of inkognytos seeds. Save the money, and buy from someone else. Dont go through what i went through. I waited for a few months for their seeds to be in stock only to finally get them and be given what appears damaged seeds. With no refund etc. Rant over.

items.name: Let's see your auto grows!
items.name_norm: let s see your auto grows
items.grow_notes:
As soon as my first grow finished up (2x2 photo scrog) I knew I wanted to add another tent and I wanted to try growing autos. I had been using one of the Mars TS1000 tent kits I ordered on Amazon for $370 primed. I put together a budget 3x3 solution on Amazon using a Vivosun tent, Vivosun ventilation kit with carbon filter, and a Maxsisun MF 2000 light for around $300 shipped.

Cheap 3x3 pros: Cost, wattage, square footage, the door opens much wider, quieter ventilation, remote control light, better driver and LEDs

TS1000 kit pros: higher quality tent, able to remotely mount the driver for more temperature control

I wanted to have four perpetual autos and planned on starting a new one every three weeks or so depending on ripeness but the Skywalker OG Auto decided she wants half of the tent so I'm stopping popping seeds until space frees up over time.

Auto tent - left: (LSD Auto - late flower, Skywalker OG - early flower, Wedding Cake Auto - seedling)

Photo tent - right: (Mimosa x Orange Punch - early flower)

items.excerpt:
Hey, folks.

Exclusively outdoor grower here, wondering about saving my own seeds.

If I have the ability to isolate a male, is it as easy as growing out both a female & male of a strain, harvesting pollen from the male, and carefully pollinating a flower or two on the female? Most of the regular seeds I'm looking at right now are from Authentic Genetics. Some are clearly hybrids (i.e. Sour Diesel x Purest Indica) but some are referred to as an Inbred Line (i.e. NL #5). Will I have better luck with either kind? My crude understanding of the process is that, even if it's within the same strain, if you're pollinating a hybrid from a hybrid, your resulting seeds will reveal all kinds of latent genetics and may not perfectly resemble the parent plants.

Alternatively, I've read a little bit about using colloidal silver to force a female plant into making pollen sacs. Is it possible for that plant, then, to self-pollinate? So long as you don't spray her down with SO much colloidal silver that you no longer have any female flowers to be pollinated? I'm particularly interested in this process as it appears to be the "path of least resistance" for lack of a better term.

Some things to note about my growing methods:

- Again, exclusively outdoor (VERY Upper Midwest.. cold af)

- For better or worse, I'm not interested in keeping mother plants alive and/or cloning. We just don't have the physical space for that.

- Similarly, I don't have the space to start dozens of plants with the intention of carrying them through to a stage that allows me to isolate for preferred traits before deciding which ones to grow out and use for pollinating. It's more likely that I'd have a couple females in my garden, a male of the same strain in a pot at a separate location, and I'd just settle for harvesting pollen from the male and then pollinating the best looking female in the bunch.

In the end, I'm mostly interested in generating some of my own seeds rather than relying on purchasing them year to year. I've identified some strains that work well in my climate and would love to start saving some of those seeds!

Thanks for your time.

items.excerpt:
Hey folks,

I wanted to keep better track of my grows and also have a place to get some feedback from the community on those grows since I'm still so new to all of this. Anyone is welcome to post on my grow journal with questions or advice. Also worth noting that all of my experience up to this point has been with autoflowers, and that this thread will only ever talk about autoflowers so please keep any advice or questions with that in mind.

This is only my third time growing cannabis, with the first time being a disaster (less than a 1/2oz dry from one plant) and my second time yielding a little over 5oz dry from two plants. Generally, I believe my problems with my first grows were overwatering and providing too many nutrients which caused the plants to get stunted. I also learned in my last grow that my water is probably too hard for my plants (around 350ppm out of the tap unfiltered) and was causing nutrient lockout from calcium abundance. I started using an old water filter I used to use for aquarium keeping to combat that issue.

Tonight I'm starting to soak my next few seeds and preparing for my next grow and will be following Budzbuddhas FFOF made simple tek as well as I can with what I have access to right now. Shoutout to @Budzbuddha for a great thread for newbies.

This time around I'll be growing in 7 gallon cloth pots, using FFOF cut with extra perlite (about 1 extra cup of perlite for every 4 cups FFOF) and amended with 1/2 a cup of Dr. Earth 4-6-3 organic & natural tomato, vegetable & herb mix on the bottom half of the pot. I've also mixed in a healthy dusting of great white mycorrhizae into several layers of the soil.

My plan is to soak my seeds for 24 hours, then place them into rapid rooters. Those will go into my seedling dome with a heating mat/light on to keep them warm (it's winter in MN right now, and I grow in my basement) until the cotyledons are free of the seed casing. I'll leave them there for a day or so longer before moving those into their 7 gallon pots, I'll dust the outside of the rapid rooter with great white mycorrhizae before placing those into their 7 gal pots.

The goal of this grow is to be as low maintenance as possible, and to not use any of the fox farm trio nutes that I'd been trying to use in previous grows. Instead, I will top dress with more FFOF/organic nutrients and water in additional mycorrhizae booster as the grow goes on.

More to come with pictures and updates.

-----

Equipment I use/setup:

2x4 ac infinity tent

ac infinity controller 69 pro

Ionboard S24 - 220W

Ionbeam S16 Supplemental grow lights

Cloudline A4 Inline fan

Carbon Filter

Cloudforge T3 Humidifier

Termoforge T3 Heater

2x cloudray s4 circulator fans

ac infinity humidity dome/heating pad (only used for starting seeds)

aquatic life ro buddie 3-stage

5-gal self watering pot bases (these are mostly used to keep the pots off the cold floor, and to catch runoff)

Water:

RO water filtered using "ro buiddie 3-stage" cut with 1/4 tap water to add a little minerals back. (we have hard water, so I have to filter to get the ppm of the water down)

Water is phd using general hydroponics ph up and ph down. 

Target PH is 6.3 - 6.4

Ventilation setup:

Air is vented from tent directly to outside air

Seeds:

ILGM - LSD autoflower

(I now know that ILGM doesn't have the best reputation for seeds, and will go elsewhere next time but I'm working with what I've got for now)

Very few seeds found, super frosty, nice spongy bud structure. I just loved it. Great flavorful smoke with easy cerebral/body effects. The others were actually pretty decent but packed with seeds. Afterwards, I noticed I had a power strip with a small light that I missed in the tent, and thought maybe it was what caused the problem. Anyway, I just gave it another try and I’m at week 4 of flower. Sure enough I’m finding little watermelons at the base of some of the lower flarfy stuff. It had a couple fully formed pollen sacks already spilling pollen. Another plant showed female pre flowers well in advance of the others, and has since showed no signs of hermie. Not really knowing squat about ge
items.excerpt:
So, I grew some seeds given to me by someone I thought of as a guru of sorts. It was supposedly from a collaborative project with some other grower. Skunk#1xMendo Rock Candy. They all hermied on me. It was mid flower and I didn’t have anything else going on, so I removed the balls/nanners and grew it out. One of the plants turned out awesome. Very few seeds found, super frosty, nice spongy bud structure. I just loved it. Great flavorful smoke with easy cerebral/body effects. The others were actually pretty decent but packed with seeds. Afterwards, I noticed I had a power strip with a small light that I missed in the tent, and thought maybe it was what caused the problem. Anyway, I just gave it another try and I’m at week 4 of flower. Sure enough I’m finding little watermelons at the base of some of the lower flarfy stuff. So, not wanting to throw in the towel like I probably should, I am curious about a few things. One of the plants showed male right away, before the flip. It had a couple fully formed pollen sacks already spilling pollen. Another plant showed female pre flowers well in advance of the others, and has since showed no signs of hermie. Not really knowing squat about genetics, I’m anecdotally guessing that both the male and female in question are not confused about their gender. If I take one of the clones (yes I kept clones from each cuz I’m touched in the head) and bred it with the male (yea I kept the male cuz I have some screws loose), can I assume that their offspring will be less likely to have the hermie gene, or would I have to run several cycles to have any real impact?

Thanks in advance for your insight, and keep in mind I’m a total hobbyist who finds enjoyment in doing things that some may consider to be, well, pretty fucking stupid, like wasting money and energy on growing shitty weed when I could just buy great genetics from reputable breeders.

items.name: Original Skunk weed from 1985 Texas
items.grow_notes: I am looking for the one and only 1985 Skunk from all over Texas. I saw this weed in high school in 1984-1985 all over Texas. This was the skunkiest weed ever. It had huge seeds 4xs the size nowdays and the were covered with big veins. Very recognizable. I clearly remember finding a few seeds and saving them and growing them in Athens, Texas in my grandparents back yard. They got about a foot tall and were killed by a lawnmower. I remember they had the widest leaf blades I have ever seen and fat stalks that were wedged like heirloom tomatoes. Our guess was it was from Afghanistan or Pakistan carried by returning GIs on cargo planes. The whole crew must have been in on it. There was so much of this stuff it flooded the state. All weed was $15-20 a quarter with panama red going for $20 an oz. The Skunk was $35 a quarter. You could smell it a long way aways. Even the small plants I had stunk. I have looked at many afghani strains like Kandahar black but not seeing what I remember. I am looking at fb afghan pakistan seeds and they look promising. any input would be appreciated

So I am a little geeked right now. Grabbed a pack of locktite today, and it's not getting rereleased so I am pretty happy to have been given a chance to grab them.

I already feel like kobain's kush and lithium og are gonna be 2 I regret not grabbing.

items.name_norm: rescue grow 3 purple kush 1 sleepy joe
items.thread_title: Rescue grow! 3 purple kush,1 sleepy joe.
items.grow_notes:
Let me start off by saying these 4 plants were rescued from a buddy's grow..his kid thought he knew the know...and well long story short, he was hitting ph of 4.8 runoff...they all had been topped and one of the PK's was missing her second apical branch, snapped off after the 1st node...so only the first node left on one side.

Started by flushing the girls with ph6.7 RO water..as of right now I dont know what he was running for nutes...im hitting around 6.4 ish now on runoff. I figured that was good enough for now. I layed them all down flat to form the table...and now its just a waiting game to see if they pop back. My buddy said they were going into week 6 of veg...which tells me they were stunted for a bit from low ph lockout or reduced uptake.

items.name: Sealed/Hybrid? Best Stealth Intake Options?
items.name_norm: sealed hybrid best stealth intake options
items.grow_notes:
Back after a few long years. Excited to get back to my passion.

I have a pristine place for my hobby again and want to maximize what’s at my disposal. Previously I’ve run a smaller space roughly 8x8 and another 12x12. Both vented grows. Had great success.

Now I’m in a 30x22 total space. There is a bathroom that is within the space in a corner of room. Bathroom is 5x3.5.

I need contain all procedures within this space. Start, finish, trim, and store. And need to accommodate each phase within its designed space.

I’m not much of a builder so was thinking incorporating a 5x10 tent for veg and the rest of the space primarily for finish with a small space alloted for processing and storage. I was leaning towards using the bathroom to for drying.

What are your thoughts? Issues? Suggestions?

Secondly, I’m thinking of going hybrid vs sealed. Thoughts?

There are windows I could set up for use for intake but what’s the best stealth method? I was going to exhaust from from bathroom vent.

How much exhaust will I need running hybrid? Can my intake be passive only? If not, how much intake? 

Can I intake only once, into the veg tent and out to flower room, and exhaust flower room only?

Y

items.grow_notes:

The strain I have takes about 8-9 weeks. I started pulling some seeds off the plants at harvest time very delicately with tweezers; the ones that looked like they were mature and ready for plucking. The genetic library to do it all was there but we took it to tropical areas selecting high thc no cbd and structure of sativa. It was brought there in its more original form but it was so harsh that the plant mutated into an auto.

To call autos ruderalis is funny because its only like one gene that determines if it autos or not and its a mutation. So its not ditch weed, its actually the most original cannabis I am thinking, that just mutated. If you removed the mutation in a vast population looking for the one that turned out photoperiod; you would of significantly purged it already by keeping photoperiod. To then breed the auto out. If you do this you should have (if this is all right) a basal breed. 

I would self the photo period assuming I will only get one, then start many different sib mate lines. Get Selfish with it. By first removing the majority of what that breed was to isolate something special. Then fall in love with all the specimens that inbreed to stabilize in each line, creating all different distinct qualities. Id avoid selfing and sib mate from the start if I can. So its ruderalis from the steppe in a place called kazakh. Its not your ordinary plant. Its a pure wild type. The seeds have water proof shell, need to mimick freeze/thaw cycle, could take over a year to sprout.. 

This one will be an advanced project. I will pop as many seeds I can to hopefully get a few males and females to sib mate. This is so I can go from having 50 seeds to 5000. Then all I do is grow them out and cull what flowers and keep the unicorn that doesnt. I would cut branches of sacs off males to store pollen so I always have pollen on stand by. They are known to sprout at various times. I need to still dive into how to make sure I dont pass on a hermaphradite as its a bit different with autos.

Besides that, uhh.. Yea.. If youve been following me on my thread “creating a flower rosin IBL” you can see where I am going with this. Transgressive segregation is when two parents crossed create a unicorn cross because their genetic blue print merged together to create something unseen in both parents. My dozens of kazakh lines can be crossed with many hybrids that create smells and tastes never seen before in cannabis. Because the other missing half of the library purged from 12k years ago come back to create the diversity we been desperate to bring back.

I would preserve earlier lines to be bred forward outdoors to retain the hearty outdoor genes nature spent millions of years perfecting. They are lost with indoor breeding because there is no natural selection pressure. Growing it outside would ensure its carrying the right genes forward while the moldy weak herming plants die off; that otherwise would of been chosen to breed with indoors. Pest resilience. That would be the breeding tool. A fresh reset. Could get strains that smell and taste metallic or like a bar of soap, dryer sheets, pocket lint.. Or that is what my varieties would be like. items.excerpt:
Il be working with TH Seeds for a while. Il be growing a pack of Watermelon Ultra 6 seeds. I may get more along with some MK Ultra too. Will post a summary of each pheno with pics. It all started with my first serious grow 2 years ago, I popped a freebie of WU and Kongs Krush. They were both keepers but the WU seeded.

 I was told and learned its basically two personalities. One from seed and from clone. From seed if can accumilate stressors that cause herms in flower. Clones can reset and not herm again if it picks your environment like mine did and become your indoor queen. She never seeded again only a couple clones from playing with light schedule instead of 12/12.

Infact going back to 12/12 is what brought my interest back into TH Seeds. They doubled flower yield from 8oz to 16oz clones. Of course not all were one pound but .85 of a pound average is great. Maybe the genetics breaking down to not yield my flower rosin at 20% anymore but 10% now average; could include more one pound plants on average or closer to it. 

I did 6 clones last run and got 5 pounds. A 10oz clone, 12.25, 13.65, 14, 15 and 16oz. Super close to 5 pounds you may as well hand it to me. Im sure a fresh pheno can easily do 15oz average. To get 1 pound I got to push her harder than ever which made it my worst looking clone. The rest were pretty good. The 10oz clone clearly had a mutant look to it and small colas.

The genetics broke down so its what I was thinking was a peak into my mothers health. I think if its new it should be consistant and was even with two very different setups. Now I got like 5 different expressions and poor results pressing them. Ive never seen such low extract yields from her hand trimming which doubled my yield from machine trimming. The machine just ruins it. I wet trim, de nug and dry herb shelf.

The flower on this pheno just doesnt smoke nice but my fam smoked it as long as I grew it had jo complaints. When you smoke a gram a day you wont notice this. Its gassy is the main scent that comes to mind when putting buds in bags ready to cure or press to flower rosin. Sticky as hell, jams my pre press mold in just a QP versus a half pound. It leans to og kush but has that g13 yield.

I wonder if its just a thing to be harsh as I grew their banana candy krush and was very similar. Grew sterile nanners and harsh smoke doesnt reak much when it dries out from handling to smoke and etc with time. The BCK was great and something to review too after I get this WU point across.

So yea, this strain has served me well. My journal is my username if you search it on the search bar on this site. It will show you everything in great detail if you just scan through photos. Like a lot of newbies, you can skip my texts until the very end as thats when a newbie turned seasoned grower starts to make harder hitting posts. Updates to take seriously. Even then, you just never know with me sometimes lol.

Pics of my pheno. The flower rosin is just this amazing og kush variant. Super gassy lemon sometimes sweet like sugar with a gassy backend. Something to die for so Im hunting for this again. The flower yield just sets a new bar along with 20% flower rosin. Its basically like having 30% pheno that only yields 10oz at best. Unicorn anyone will agree. I was told when starting out flower rosin Id need to hope to find my micheal jordan.

Well I found her first try and grew clones 7 times so 8 grows with this gal. Never seeds. All I need to do is find this again but it cannot seed from seed. So her genetic tendancy to herm is low in both seed and clones. Thats what you want to breed with. Sterile breeding seems to be a debatable option as she threw sterile nanners.

 I want to make a flower rosin IBL of the unicorn if I find her. Im just reviewing their gear before it becomes my own. Breeding is fun. Going to pop 3 WU to start vegging for next grow pretty soon here. I already flipped all plants for this run.

The most exciting thing about legalization and pot in modern times, is the emergence of seed companies like the Real Seed Company. Opening up access to genetics many of which I had never heard of. Stuff that is exciting in the boring flat buzz purple candy gas weed of today.

 I ordered some C99 from them and really was excited to see what freebies Angus would send. Baboom! He sent 25 Nepalese Mountain Ganga seeds.And a 5 pack of the Afghan mix.

 Before now the smallest seeds I ever saw were Dutch grown- Williams Wonder. These seeds are wonderfully tiny. I know this is special herb. I'm stoked to have actual Afghani seeds too. Osama Bong Loadin' in the house.

This will be my attempt at fully documenting a mixed grow with the intention of finding the best phenos from the seeds I am planting. 

I say “attempt” because I’ve seen so many incomplete grow journals that I have to wonder if I have what it takes to see it all the way through, lol!

The breeder strains are as follows:

3 LVTK x Longbottom fighter (Bad dawg genetics, freebies from GLG)

3 Rockstar Kush (BC Bud Depot)

3 Chem 91 (Shoreline genetics)

All seeds have been soaked and then placed in paper towels and today most of them were showing their tap roots.

I planted 2 of the 3 Rockstar, 2 of the 3 Chem 91 and 3 of the 3 Bad Dawg.

I also planted 27 of the 30 LSD Poison X and 27 of the 30 Bubblegum X.

Expecting a large variety in the plants, so choosing favourites might be tough, but currently aiming to keep about six at most.

Will post some pics soon, although not much to look at right now, lol!

items.name: Why I'll avoid Autoflower seeds.
items.name_norm: why i ll avoid autoflower seeds
items.grow_notes:
In my opinion Autoflower are pure gimmick marketing fluff claiming "Faster Harvests!" And "Beginner friendly!" In reality I am finding that they take just as long to go from seed to harvest and they are not nearly as forgiving as photoperiod plants. Let's break it down here.

A few people I've talked to say they hit the marketed harvest window with little to no amber trichomes for Autoflower plants, not a big deal unless they are marketing and bragging about how fast the seed to harvest is right? Maybe I'm wrong... What are your experiences?

Another thing is with a photoperiod you can high stress train, have issues, and rebound until it's healthy enough to flip to 12/12 if you want to. You decide when the plant flowers. items.excerpt:
In my opinion Autoflower are pure gimmick marketing fluff claiming "Faster Harvests!" And "Beginner friendly!" In reality I am finding that they take just as long to go from seed to harvest and they are not nearly as forgiving as photoperiod plants. Let's break it down here.

A few people I've talked to say they hit the marketed harvest window with little to no amber trichomes for Autoflower plants, not a big deal unless they are marketing and bragging about how fast the seed to harvest is right? Maybe I'm wrong... What are your experiences?

Another thing is with a photoperiod you can high stress train, have issues, and rebound until it's healthy enough to flip to 12/12 if you want to. You decide when the plant flowers. With autos if you high stress train and the plant decides to flower because it's an auto you might not be able to recover.

With photoperiod plants you can buy one seed, turn it into a mother and clone it for mass runs. You can't clone autoflowers can you? You certainly can't make them mothers unless someone is doing it and there's a technique I haven't heard about.

With photoperiod plants you can leave a few bud sites and reveg a good phenotype and then turn it into a mother for clones. Can't do that with autoflower plants either.

Here's Barney's Farm Watermelon Z auto day 98 in the front from planting as a seed with zero ambers about 40% clear trichomes.

items.name: Your latest seed purchase?
items.grow_notes:
What's your latest? What was your reasoning?

Just sent 650 bucks to Sannie to pick up some 2 more packs of Sugar Punch, a bunch of Jack Herer seeds (4 packs reg and 2 packs fem), 2 packs of Caramel Cough, 2 packs of Shackzilla and a pack of Columbian Gold x Lambsbread.

Why? I love sativas. And Sannie has fantastic sativas. I wanted to do Caramel Cough one run but fucked up and let them all die because I left a fan near them while they were still in rockwool which dried them out quick.

Also picked up from the tude:

2 packs of Peyote Purple from Cannabiogen - because it's supposed to be fucking amazing and I see nothing but incredibly beautiful flower pictures. I'm hoping for a male as they come out of this line in low numbers, but if I don't get one I won't cry about it.

1 pack of Zamaldelica non fem from CBG. I know the fem is rated more highly but I want to fuck around and do some breeding with it to bring out some more pure phenotypes in F2's. This is a longer term project though.

1 single C99 seed from female seeds because everyone loves it and I like C99 and I had to max out the 250 dollar prepaid. It'll probably get run eventually.
